None of the three proposed values matches what I recall for this result, so I'm answering NONE. This rests on memory of the literature, not a derivation, and I have not checked it against the paper.

I recall the critical moment for the divisible sandpile with i.i.d. masses of mean μ < 1 on infinite bounded-degree graphs being q = 2. Stabilization is guaranteed for a finite p-th moment with p > 2, and for every p < 2 there are graphs and mass distributions that explode.

The three solutions give q ≈ 2.6067 (Solution 1), q = 3 (Solution 2), and q = 1 + ln 2 ≈ 1.693 (Solution 3). None of these equals 2. Each argument also rests on heuristic exponent computations that I could not verify from the sketches given.

CHOICE: NONE
